The two congruent sides together are 2 × 22 = 44 feet. The third side is the rest of the perimeter: 78 − 44 = 34 feet. Choice A assumes all three sides are 22, which would give a perimeter of only 66.
Force is the product of mass and acceleration, so F = 41 × a = 41a. Choices B, C and D add or subtract the mass and acceleration instead of multiplying them.

In f(t) = 28,000(2)^t, setting t = 0 gives f(0) = 28,000, so 28,000 is the number of bacteria at the initial measurement. One hour later there would be 56,000, not 28,000, so choice C is wrong; the doubling every hour comes from the base 2.

Because lines l and k are parallel, the angle x at line l equals the angle at line k on the same side of t, and that angle together with y forms a straight line. So x + y = 180 and y = 180 − x. If x > 165, then y < 180 − 165 = 15. Choices C and D are false because x + y is exactly 180.
Combine like terms: 7x^4 + 10x^4 − 10x^4 = (7 + 10 − 10)x^4 = 7x^4. So b = 7.

Doubling every day means multiplying by 2 for each day, starting from 72,000. So y = 72,000(2)^t. Choice C uses a base of 1/2, which models halving, and choices A and B raise 72,000 to the power t instead of 2.

The two lines have different slopes (1 and 5), so they are not parallel and cross at exactly one point. Solving x + 15 = 5x gives x = 15/4, the single intersection. Two distinct lines can never meet at exactly 2 or 5 points.
In the form (x − h)^2 + (y − k)^2 = b, the center is (h, k). The center is (5, 1), so h = 5 (and b = 7^2 = 49).
For angle X, the opposite side is YZ = 222 and the adjacent side is XZ = 296. So tan X = 222/296 = 3/4 (dividing both by 74). Choice A (4/3) is the reciprocal, which is tan Y.
